title: Merge notify and update-context into single call
description:
Every worker completion currently requires 2 separate commands:
1. `tf.py notify worker bead --context-pct N --summary "..."`
2. `tf.py update-context --bead bead --worker worker --summary "..." --files "f1,f2" --gotcha "..."`

Merge them: add `--files` and `--gotcha` optional flags to `notify` (cmd_notify, tf.py:570-651). When `--files` is provided, call the same logic as `update-context` (the `_append_to_section` calls from cmd_update_context at tf.py:1540-1590) internally after updating the registry.

Keep `update-context` as a standalone command for manual orchestrator notes.

Also add `--files` to `batch-notify` (cmd_batch_notify, tf.py:654-696) — apply to the last bead in each pair.

Update the argparse registration for `notify` and `batch-notify` to include the new flags.

Add test cases:
- `notify` with `--files` triggers context update
- `notify` with `--files` and `--gotcha` writes both
- `notify` without `--files` behaves exactly as before (no context update)
- `batch-notify` with `--files` applies to context

Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py`, `treeflow/test_tf.py`
acceptance_criteria:
- `tf.py notify worker-1 bead-1 --context-pct 45 --summary "added auth" --files "src/auth.rs,src/main.rs"` updates both registry AND context file in one call
- `tf.py notify` without `--files` works exactly as before
- All existing notify tests still pass
close_reason: SUMMARY: Added --files and --gotcha flags to notify and batch-notify. When --files provided, context update logic runs inline.. FILES: treeflow/tf.py,treeflow/test_tf.py. CONTEXT: 15%

title: Trim ready command output to essential fields
description:
The `ready` command (tf.py:1092-1125) passes through raw bead objects from `bd` without trimming. Each bead from bd contains `created_at`, `updated_at`, `labels`, `assignee`, full `description`, etc. A 10-bead ready list could be 3000+ tokens when trimmed it would be ~300.

This is the single largest token waste in tf.py (per the token efficiency audit).

Fix: After fetching beads from bd, trim each to only: `id`, `title`, `type`, `priority`, `parent`, `status`. Drop everything else.

Also fix duplicate fields in ready output: `capped` and `capped_count` duplicate `supplemented`. Remove `capped` and `capped_count` — just `supplemented` suffices.

Add/update tests in `TestReady` to verify trimmed output shape.

Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py`, `treeflow/test_tf.py`
acceptance_criteria:
- `ready` output bead objects contain only `id`, `title`, `type`, `priority`, `parent`, `status`
- No `created_at`, `updated_at`, `labels`, `assignee`, `description` in output
- `capped` and `capped_count` removed from output
- Existing ready tests updated and passing
close_reason: SUMMARY: Trimmed ready output to 6 essential fields (id,title,type,priority,parent,status), mapped issue_type->type, removed capped/capped_count duplicates. AC: met. FILES: treeflow/tf.py,treeflow/test_tf.py. CONTEXT: 15%

title: Make notify bead-id optional with registry lookup
description:
`tf.py dispatch` already records the bead ID in the worker's registry entry. But `notify` requires it as a positional arg, forcing the orchestrator to extract it from `<task-notification>` text.

Make `bead_id` an optional positional arg in `notify`. When omitted, look up the worker's current `bead` from the registry. Fail with a clear error if the worker has no bead recorded.

In the argparse registration, change `bead_id` from a required positional to `nargs='?'` with `default=None`.

Add test cases:
- `notify worker-1 --context-pct 45 --summary "done"` (no bead_id) looks up bead from registry
- `notify worker-1 bead-1 --context-pct 45 --summary "done"` (with bead_id) works as before
- `notify unknown-worker --context-pct 45 --summary "done"` (no bead_id, unknown worker) fails with error

Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py`, `treeflow/test_tf.py`
acceptance_criteria:
- `notify` with bead_id omitted resolves it from registry
- `notify` with bead_id provided uses the provided value (backward compatible)
- Error message when worker not found and no bead_id is clear
close_reason: SUMMARY: Made bead_id optional positional in notify. Registry lookup with clear error when worker has no bead.. FILES: treeflow/tf.py,treeflow/test_tf.py. CONTEXT: 20%

title: Harden conflict-check file extraction regex

Extend the regex to also accept:
- `Files to create/modify:` and `Files to <verb>:` patterns
- `Modified files:`, `Changed files:`, `Target files:` as synonyms

Also extend `_extract_files_detailed()` (tf.py:818-839) with the same pattern improvements.

Add test cases in `TestConflictCheckHelpers` covering:

- `Files to change: src/c.rs`
- `Modified files: src/d.rs`
- `Target files: src/e.rs`
- `Changed files: src/f.rs`

- `_extract_files_from_description("Target files: src/x.rs")` returns `["src/x.rs"]`
- All existing tests still pass

title: Support batch dispatch with comma-separated beads
description:
Currently dispatching a worker with 2 beads requires 2 `tf.py dispatch` calls. Support comma-separated bead IDs: `tf.py dispatch worker-1 bead-1,bead-2 --skill domain`.

In `cmd_dispatch` (tf.py:251-275):
1. Split `args.bead_id` on comma
2. Store as a list in the registry entry's `bead` field (or store the first and add a `beads` list field)
3. Set `notification: "pending"` as before

For backward compatibility, keep the single-bead case storing a plain string. When multiple beads, store as a list.

Add test cases:

- Dispatch with single bead stores string (backward compat)
- `notify` with worker that has multiple beads uses the provided bead_id

Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py`, `treeflow/test_tf.py`

- Existing dispatch tests pass
close_reason: SUMMARY: Added comma-separated bead support to dispatch. Single bead=string, multiple=list. AC: all met. FILES: treeflow/tf.py,treeflow/test_tf.py. CONTEXT: 50%

title: Remove redundant fields from conflict-check, validate-plan, status, sync, notify
description:
Per the token efficiency audit, several commands emit redundant or unnecessary fields:

**conflict-check** (tf.py:856-941):
- Remove `bead_files` from output (line 919). The orchestrator only needs `conflicts`, `safe_parallel`, and `serial_groups`. The per-bead file lists are diagnostic.
- Rename `safe_parallel` to `safe`, `serial_groups` to `serial` (shorter keys)

**validate-plan** (tf.py:1233-1382):
- Remove `dry_run` field (line 1381) — orchestrator already has the plan file
- Remove `missing_files` field — duplicates entries in `errors`
- Remove `orphan_packages` field — duplicates entries in `warnings`

**status** (tf.py:2130-2185):
- Remove `stalled_action` field (line 2182) — 76-char instructional string the orchestrator already knows from SKILL.md
- Remove `failed: 0` from worker counts when zero

**sync** (tf.py:2027-2127):
- Simplify `retired_now` to a list of worker name strings instead of objects with reason codes. The orchestrator doesn't need to know WHY a worker was retired.
- Remove `addressable` from counts — redundant with idle workers that have low `idle_min`

**notify** (tf.py:570-651):
- Omit `late: false` on the common path (line 613). Only include `late` key when true.
- Omit `auto_closed`, `auto_retired`, `parent_auto_closed` when false/absent — only include when true.

**worker-close** (tf.py:278-443):
- Remove `hint` fields from error responses (lines 331, 351, 345). Errors are self-explanatory.

**Shorten verbose error/warning strings:**
- Line 1289: shorten to `"unrecognized H3: {header}"`
- Line 1356: shorten to `"'{title}' missing Files:"`
- Line 1350: shorten to `"fully sequential — no parallelism"`

Update all affected tests to match new output shapes.

Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py`, `treeflow/test_tf.py`
acceptance_criteria:
- `conflict-check` no longer emits `bead_files`; uses `safe` and `serial` as key names
- `validate-plan` no longer emits `dry_run`, `missing_files`, or `orphan_packages`
- `status` no longer emits `stalled_action`
- `sync` `retired_now` is a flat list of names
- `notify` omits falsy boolean fields
- All tests updated and passing
close_reason: SUMMARY: Removed redundant fields from 6 commands. Updated all affected tests. AC: all criteria met. FILES: treeflow/tf.py,treeflow/test_tf.py. CONTEXT: 35%

title: Add --parallel-with flag to worker-prompt
description:

Add `--parallel-with bead1,bead2` flag to `worker-prompt` (cmd_worker_prompt, tf.py:1770-1956). When set:
1. For each bead in `--parallel-with`, call `_extract_files_from_description()` on its description
2. Append a "Parallel Worker Warning" H2 section to the generated prompt listing each file with the bead that owns it, and a note to call `tf.py block` if the worker needs those files.

Add to argparse: `--parallel-with` as an optional string arg (comma-separated bead IDs).

Add test cases:
- `worker-prompt --beads id1 --parallel-with id2,id3` includes warning section
- `worker-prompt --beads id1` (no --parallel-with) has no warning section
- Warning section lists correct files from parallel beads

title: Fix shell injection via unsanitized user strings in subprocess calls
description:
Refactor all locations where user-controlled strings are interpolated into shell commands via f-strings passed to `subprocess.run(shell=True)`. Use `shlex.quote()` for all user-provided strings: bead titles, question text, close reasons, descriptions, summaries. Affected locations: `tf.py:404` (close reason), `tf.py:497` (question/context in bd create), `tf.py:523` (title/desc in bd create), `tf.py:656` (auto-close reason), `tf.py:1377` (close reason). Currently only `"` is escaped with `replace('"', '\\"')` which does not prevent injection via `$(...)`, backticks, or other shell metacharacters. Replace all manual `replace('"', '\\"')` escaping with `shlex.quote()`. Note: `shlex` is already imported at line 10. Also audit any other `_run()` calls that interpolate non-constant strings.
Acceptance: All user-provided strings passed to `_run()` are wrapped with `shlex.quote()`. No `replace('"', '\\"')` pattern remains. Tests pass.
Files (modifies): `treeflow/tf.py` [cmd_worker_close, cmd_block, cmd_discover, cmd_notify, cmd_close]
close_reason: auto-closed on worker notification

title: Extract _fetch_bead helper and deduplicate bead-fetching pattern
description:

Create a `_fetch_bead(bd: str, bid: str) -> Optional[dict]` helper that encapsulates this pattern: runs `bd show {bid} --json`, parses JSON, handles list-vs-dict response, and returns the bead dict or None on failure. Replace all inline instances with calls to this helper.
Acceptance: A single `_fetch_bead()` helper exists. All 8+ call sites use it. No inline `bd show --json` + JSON parse + list-unwrap pattern remains. Tests pass.
